answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 slots of dedicated service capacity at a global registrar to maintain a verified presence, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each identity acts like a raven seeking a unique roost within the network. A verifier monitors the comet path of incoming requests for overlap; any sonnet of repeated signals triggers a permanent prune. Honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal costs.
